[b]The Union of the Strong[/b]
King Erjk Drs stood at the window of the Drspalatze overlooking the great square of St. Ateling, the distant sound of the bells of the monastery Klaren ringing out over the city. However, his mind was not upon the bells or the view of the tourists and sellers in the square below, but upon the union. 

For the past decade he had headed a secret commission founded by his mother, which sought to bring Thýven and the states of High Albany, Averne, and Hitherlands into a formal political union. It was the ultimate form of shadow government, hidden away from the constitution fearing legislature and supreme court. Erjk had quietly moved deals and pawns across the table. It had first started with small gestures of unity, cultural events, occasional funding of a new hospital or company in the states across the strait. Then the occasional military drill training program, then industrial and economic deals for trade reinforcing ancient deals from centuries prior. 

In Erjks eyes, despite the varied species difference between the citizens of the states across the strait, the two nations had always been one through history. Now as the efforts of the commission began to yield results, he had ordered the chairman of the commission to prepare a formal report for public consumption. 

The question was now, whether the idea would be received well, he already knew the general opinion of those across the strait, it was optimistic at best. However, with the number of war-heavy and unstable nations across the world, the union could stand as a symbol and bastion of strength in the Western hemisphere. With power centres in the East. 

Of course there would be the attempted copycats, those who would try to place the mantle of union upon their own heads, but the tradition and history would not be there, and thus, they would be made into fools. 

Erjk moved from the window, the light hitting his curving antlers, It shall be done, he said to himself.

A knock disturbed him from his musing as he permitted the door to open, it was the chairman of the commission, and before him, a thick book wrapped in red velvet, the title glimmering off the cover. 

Ah! It is done, stated Erjk a little too enthusiastically, for though he was indeed enthusiastic. 

Yes, the entire report, 1,200 pages of our work and deeds, replied the chairman, bowing.

When will it be released to the general public? enquired Erjk as he lifted the cover to look over the title page and chapters.

Tomorrow, in a more readable format, I believe it is 600 pages the public one, replied the chairman.

And the one for the Gøsfodde? asked Erjk.

The same one which you hold, it will be released to the individual legislators today, I have my couriers running around with the copies, replied the Chairman.

Good, good, I thank you for your effort, replied Erjk, smiling as he closed the book.

Of course your majesty, replied the chairman, By the way, have you chosen a new title? he asked.

Yes, but it shall not be revealed until the formal unification is committed, replied Erjk.

Very good, replied the chairman, Well then, I shall be on my way, he stated, stepping out of the room.

Erjk nodded politely as he once again turned his attention to the velvet and gold bound book, caressing it gently he smiled once again, Yes, it shall be done, he repeated to himself. 

[nation]Averne[/nation]
